source_item.title: Dollar at 3-month lows after weekly slump; yen set to halt post-intervention slide

card.what_happened: The US dollar has weakened significantly, reaching a three-month low against major currencies. This decline follows a week of selling pressure, while the Japanese yen shows signs of stabilizing after recent intervention.
card.what_happened_verbose: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the dollar's strength against a basket of major currencies, has experienced a notable slump, hitting its lowest point in three months. This broad-based dollar weakness is attributed to various factors, including shifting interest rate expectations and potentially reduced demand for safe-haven assets. Concurrently, the Japanese yen appears to be halting its slide, suggesting that recent currency intervention efforts may be having some effect.
